en.title: Land Office Is Delaying Your Service
en.directAnswer: First identify the exact land service and check its official status. The Ministry of Land portal provides mutation, land development tax, records/maps and other services. Save application and payment details. If an eligible service delay remains unresolved, use the land authority’s complaint route or GRS where appropriate.

atAGlance.whoFor: A citizen has a delay in mutation, record, map, tax or another land service.
atAGlance.legalBasis: Ministry of Land service rules; e-Mutation process; GRS.
atAGlance.mainRule: Do not use a general complaint route to replace a statutory review/appeal from an actual legal decision.
atAGlance.updateStatus: Re-check Ministry land-service hotline and complaint workflow on publication date.

en.lawMeaning: Do not use a general complaint route to replace a statutory review/appeal from an actual legal decision. This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Use the service’s review route if a decision was made.
Use grievance route for eligible delay/service-quality issues.
evidence: Application; receipt; notice; order; screenshot; office communication.
en.simpleExample: A mutation application is rejected for missing evidence. That is different from an unexplained delay. The first step is to understand the rejection and proper review route.
commonMistakes: Common mistakes: using GRS instead of appeal.
